scope: Narrow closure of storage_review_r1 S1 and subsequent after-lock/during-build source-stability concerns. Does not replace packed48 quantization review, campaign review, stack review or core numerical qualification. No implementation changes or new behavioral tests.

reviewed_control_flow.evidence: prepare recomputes all DEPENDENCIES hashes after exclusive flock and replaces expected.sources. A wait behind another cooperating builder cannot retain the pre-lock source snapshot.

Existing binary requires build.json; configuration equality includes variant and dependency hashes; actual rowwise.so bytes are SHA256-checked against the saved artifact hash. Mismatch raises rather than silently rebuilding/relabeling.
After successful generate/compile, current dependency hashes must equal the after-lock snapshot before build.json is written. An unbound artifact left by failure is refused on the next prepare call.
Both paths rehash dependencies again immediately before leaving the lock; ordinary source edits during validation raise.

Native.build_identity reads the validated build.json. RowwiseBackend.configuration_id uses its configuration.sources and binary_sha256 rather than freshly hashing possibly unrelated current source files. Parent configuration digest and explicit math/map/history_bits remain included.

Generation, compilation, receipt writing and cache validation are serialized by the same per-variant flock. Existing valid binaries are not replaced by prepare; this supports reading identity/loading after lock release for cooperating callers under the immutable artifact contract.

limitations: Source inspection closure only, as requested; it does not claim new executed tampering/race tests. storage_review_r1 remains the authority for its quantization controls.

Build/source tree is assumed frozen for import/build/use, with non-adversarial cooperating cache users. Pre/post content hashes are not a transactional filesystem snapshot and cannot detect a source file changed then restored entirely between checks. Python module code already imported from an older revision is not rebound by hashing its current disk file.

Out-of-band deletion/replacement of manifests or binaries after lock release is outside the cooperating immutable cache contract. The review does not claim protection against arbitrary external writers.
Historical campaign manifests remain historical identities; later source fixes do not retroactively relabel their binaries or result provenance.

resource_subtotal_sanity.scope: Arithmetic and wording checked only. This is a subtotal of measured components for this implementation, excluding other instructions. It is not a universal lower bound or a complete target-memory proof. The648-byte stack is an exercised witness, not a worst-case bound.
